3400100100.name: Absecon City
3400100100.summary: In Absecon City, Atlantic County, the typical home is worth about $286,000. Owning it costs about $24,700 a year, including the average property tax bill of $6,000, which is 32% of the county's median household income. That ranks 204th of 561 New Jersey municipalities for ownership affordability, where 1st is the most affordable. The median rent is $1,810 a month, or 28% of the county's median household income, which ranks 490th of 548 for rental affordability. 65% of renter households here pay 30% or more of their income on rent. A four-person household earning HUD's low-income limit for the area ($87,000 a year) could afford both the typical home's ownership costs and the median rent. Absecon City's Fourth Round prospective need, as calculated by the state in October 2024, is 22 affordable units (6.2 per 1,000 households), plus a present need of 39. The home value is the Census Bureau's ACS 2020-2024 median of what owners estimate their homes are worth, not a current market price.

3400102080.name: Atlantic City

Owning it costs about $17,700 a year, including the average property tax bill of $4,200, which is 23% of the county's median household income. Atlantic City is one of the most affordable municipalities in New Jersey in which to own a home. Atlantic City is a Qualified Urban Aid municipality, so it has no prospective need obligation under the state's Affordable Housing Law; its present need, as calculated by the state in October 2024, is 875 units. Owning it costs about $90,500 a year, including the average property tax bill of $25,100, which is 72% of the county's median household income. That ranks 518th of 561 New Jersey municipalities for ownership affordability, where 1st is the most affordable. Tenafly Borough is one of the least affordable municipalities in New Jersey in which to own a home. The median rent is $3,500 a month, or 34% of the county's median household income, which ranks 527th of 548 for rental affordability. It is one of the least affordable municipalities in New Jersey in which to rent. 36% of renter households here pay 30% or more of their income on rent. A four-person household earning HUD's low-income limit for the area ($108,000 a year) could afford neither the typical home's ownership costs nor the median rent. Tenafly Borough's Fourth Round prospective need, as calculated by the state in October 2024, is 297 affordable units (56.8 per 1,000 households), plus a present need of 68. Estimates for this town are based on limited data (rental: the Census reports only that the median rent is at least $3,500). The home value is the Census Bureau's ACS 2020-2024 median of what owners estimate their homes are worth, not a current market price.

That ranks 14th of 561 New Jersey municipalities for ownership affordability, where 1st is the most affordable. Pemberton Township is one of the most affordable municipalities in New Jersey in which to own a home. The median rent is $1,340 a month, or 15% of the county's median household income, which ranks 67th of 548 for rental affordability. 45% of renter households here pay 30% or more of their income on rent. A four-person household earning HUD's low-income limit for the area ($98,200 a year) could afford both the typical home's ownership costs and the median rent. Pemberton Township's Fourth Round prospective need, as calculated by the state in October 2024, is 79 affordable units (8.1 per 1,000 households), plus a present need of 79. The home value is the Census Bureau's ACS 2020-2024 median of what owners estimate their homes are worth, not a current market price.
